newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - rising home sales hit prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - rising home sales hit prices.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices fell from one-eight to one-quarter of a point, depressed by a surprising surge in new home sales, which soared to their highest level in more than a decade.

But traders noted that institutional activity was farily light, though there was some retail buying. As has been the case for the past year and a half or so, individuals evidently were buying cash municipal bonds instead of depositing their funds in municipal bond funds.
This phenomenon appears to reflect concerns about potential tax changes, they explained.

Sales of new single-family homes jumped 4.7 percent in August to a seasonally adjusted, annual pace of 832,000 units, the highest level since April 1986. Economists polled by Reuters had expected an annual pace of 744,000 units.
Another negative sign was seen in the Chicago Purchasing Purchasing Mangement Index, as the prices paid index climbed to 59.3 percent in September from 51.8 percent in the August.
Despite the market's retreat, which echoed a move down by the benchmark U.S. Treasury bonds, traders noted that the municipal market revealed a fairly strong appetite for new issues.
They included a $128 million issue by Orange County, Florida, Health Facilities Authority.

This led to some optimism as traders looked ahead to some of the new issues expected this week. The negotiated calender includes a $270 million sale by Denver City and County Airport, a $152 million sale by New York State Dormitory Authority, and a $150 million sale by Connecticut.
The Blue List, a gauge of the secondary market complied by Standard & Poor's Corp, stands at just over $1.1 billion, which is considered a moderate amount of supply.

The spread between municipal and Treasury bond futures stood at 152 ticks. The December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade fell six ticks to 113-30/32, while the December Treasury bond futures fell nine ticks to 109-6/32.

Actively quoted issues included Metroplitan Pier and Exposition Authority Illinois of June 2027, which carry a 5-1/4 percent NET coupon. These issues were bid at 5.85 percent, up five basis points from levels seen on Friday.
And Alliance Airport Authority Income Texas bonds of April 2021, which have a 6-7/8 percent coupon, were bid at 99, up one-quarter of a point from Friday.
